title: Heron's Formula: Area of a Triangle

meta_desc: Class 9 Heron's Formula worksheet (NCERT Chapter 10): semi-perimeter, area of a triangle from three sides, isosceles and equilateral triangles, quadrilaterals and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter.
body_html:
How it works

Heron's formula gives the area of a triangle from its three sides a, b, c: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter.

It is useful when the height is not known. A quadrilateral can be split by a diagonal into two triangles; add their areas.

Example

Find the area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm.

s = 21

√(21 × 8 × 7 × 6) = √7056

Answer: 84 cm²

Example

Find the area of an equilateral triangle of side 10 cm.

s = 15

√(15 × 5 × 5 × 5)

Answer: 25√3 cm²

Common mistakes

  • Using the perimeter instead of the semi-perimeter s.
  • Forgetting the square root at the end.
  • Using ½ × base × slant side as if the slant side were the height.

faq.a: The area of a triangle with sides a, b, c is √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s = (a + b + c)/2.

faq.q: When should I use Heron's formula?
faq.a: When you know all three sides of a triangle but not its height.
Half of the perimeter: s = (a + b + c)/2.

faq.q: How do I find the area of a quadrilateral using Heron's formula?
faq.a: Draw a diagonal to split it into two triangles, find each area with Heron's formula, and add them.
